title: The peacemakers (Matthew 5:9)
hookLine: peacemakers, not peacekeepers: they make peace where there wasn't any
carry: make peace, not just keep it

cards: Plenty of families have a peacekeeper. The one who changes the subject when politics comes up at dinner. Who says, let's not get into it.
Who smooths things over so nobody storms out. It's a real gift, and often an exhausting one. But under a kept peace, the problem is often still there.
The two brothers still aren't speaking. The old hurt still sits in the corner. The seventh line of the sermon doesn't bless the peacekeepers.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God." The Greek word is eirenopoioi. Eirene is peace; poieo is to make, to build.
Peace-makers: people who build a peace that wasn't there before. And behind it is the Hebrew shalom. Shalom isn't just no fighting.
It's wholeness: everything in its right place, nothing missing, nothing broken. So a peacemaker doesn't just stop the shouting. They go into the broken place and help build something whole.
That's harder. It usually means naming what's wrong, listening to both sides, and taking some heat, often from both sides at once.
And remember the world Jesus said this in: a land under Rome, whose Pax Romana, the Roman peace, was kept by legions and crosses.
Jesus blesses a different kind: peace that's made, not enforced.
The promise: they shall be called the children of God. In Hebrew idiom, the son of something shares its character.
Peacemakers are called God's children because they're doing what, Christians say, God does: making peace between people who were apart.
Paul would later put the practical version this way: "If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men." It takes two to make peace. But you can do your half.

how: Christians work at peacemaking through mediation between neighbors and reconciliation between communities; for the historic peace churches, such as Mennonites and Quakers, it sits at the center of their life.

o: people who build peace where there wasn't any
people who settle quarrels as judges in a court
people who keep things calm by dodging every fight

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.

s: Paul tells Christians to live peaceably, as far as it lies with them
Romans 12:18: if it be possible, as much as lieth in you.
a peacemaker is someone who avoids conflict
they build peace where there wasn't any, which often means facing conflict.
shalom means only the absence of fighting
it means wholeness: nothing missing, nothing broken.

games.q: at a family dinner, two relatives haven't spoken in a year. what does a peacemaker, not a peacekeeper, do?
o: change the subject so nobody fights.
quietly help them start to talk and mend it.
take one side to end it faster.
games.why: peacemakers build peace where there wasn't any. keeping the peace smooths things over; making it helps mend what's broken.

practice: Think of a relationship with a quiet cold war, not a battle, just a chill: someone you avoid, something unsaid.

Picture them and ask what your half of making peace would be: an apology, asking are we okay, a friendly message after a long silence, the smallest real step. If you pray, you can pray for them, and for courage.

wordCard.voice: The peacemakers. Eirenopoioi, peace builders: people who make shalom where there wasn't any, and are called the children of God.

orig.note: Greek: peacemakers. eirene, peace, and poieo, to make. Matthew 5:9.

carryVoice: Your line: make peace, not just keep it. A peacemaker builds; a peacekeeper smooths. See you on the hillside tomorrow.

sources.q: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.
